articles.title: Sixers movie night: LeBron James uses ‘I Play Rocky’ to bring teammates closer
articles.summary: LeBron James has won four NBA championships, collected four MVP awards and spent more than two decades learning what it takes to build a title-winning team. Now, as he begins a new chapter with the Philadelphia 76ers, the NBA legend is showing that leadership is about more than what happens during practice and games. James recently organized a movie night with several of his Sixers teammates, taking them to see I Play Rocky, which arrived in theaters on November 20th. The outing offered the players a chance to connect away from the basketball court while watching a film whose central themes of determination, ambition and overcoming the odds fit naturally with the mentality required to pursue an NBA championship. The gesture quickly caught the attention of basketball fans, particularly those who see it as another example of James embracing his role as a veteran leader in Philadelphia.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama invents a new NBA move after painful finger blister makes dunking difficult
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama has spent the early stages of the 2026-27 NBA season reminding everyone that there are very few things a 7-foot-4 basketball player with his skill set cannot do. Now, he has apparently invented a new way to score because one of the things he does best — dunking — has become too painful. The San Antonio Spurs star debuted what he called the “shunk,” a combination of a jump shot and a dunk, during Thursday night’s 124-112 victory over the Los Angeles Clippers. The unusual finish was born out of necessity: a painful blister on the middle finger of his right hand has made throwing down powerful dunks increasingly uncomfortable. It is an unusual problem for a player who leads the NBA in dunks, but Wembanyama found a solution that was as inventive as it was entertaining.

articles.title: LeBron James' Sixers team has one trait that could make them invincible in the NBA Playoffs
articles.standfirst: The Philadelphia 76ers are now 14-3 with a two game lead over everyone else in the Eastern Conference.
articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers are now 14-3 with a two game lead over everyone else in the Eastern Conference.
articles.body:
It wasn't the prettiest win for the Philadelphia 76ers on Saturday, but overcoming a 50-point masterpiece from Tyler Herro and edging out a 132-129 victory still warrants some respect. Especially because it has now put the Sixers two games ahead of everyone else in the Eastern Conference .

In the win over the Milwaukee Bucks , Philadelphia got double-digit scoring nights from seven different players. Joel Embiid led the way with 26 points, while LeBron James had a vintage line of 21 points, six rebounds, six assists, three steals, and one block. The amount of different contributors surely has head coach Nick Nurse feeling confident going forward.

Philadelphia 76ers are undefeated so far in "clutch games" this season

While the NBA Playoffs are still a long way away, the Sixers have already put together a resume this season that should surely translate to postseason success. There's one specific area that the Sixers are excelling in, which should theoretically come in handy during the playoffs: they're currently unbeatable in close games.

The NBA shared a stunning stat about this season's 76ers team following their victory over the Bucks: Philadelphia is 12-0 in games where they trailed or led by five points or less in the final five minutes of fourth quarter or overtime . More impressively, they've won those close games on 12 of 14 occasions, with the other two being bigger margins of victory.

Clearly, the Sixers don't get flustered in close games . That's a crucial trait come playoff time, given that most games during that instance are close. Being able to perform under pressure will be paramount, and LeBron's Sixers appear to thrive in those moments.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama channels Wilt Chamberlain with historic 50-point performance
articles.standfirst: The San Antonio Spurs beat the New Orleans Pelicans 114-91 on the back of Wemby.
articles.summary: The San Antonio Spurs beat the New Orleans Pelicans 114-91 on the back of Wemby.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama had 50 points , with 32 coming in the first half, along with 19 rebounds , five blocks and four steals and the San Antonio Spurs rolled to a 114-91 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Saturday.

Wembanyama is the first player with 30 points, 10 rebounds, three blocks and three steals in a game this season and he did so by halftime.

Stephon Castle added 19 points, six assists and three rebounds for San Antonio, which has won 14 of 15 to join the Los Angeles Lakers atop the Western Conference at 14-3.

Jeremiah Fears had 29 points and Jordan Poole added 25 points in New Orleans' third consecutive loss.

Wembanyama exited shortly after reaching 50 points on a 3-pointer that put San Antonio up 108-82 with 6:29 remaining in the game. He finished two points shy of the career high he set Nov. 4 against Dallas.

Dylan Harper missed his second straight game with a strained left hip suffered on Tuesday against Detroit in San Antonio’s lone loss since Oct. 23. The Spurs limited their turnovers to 13 after committing a season-high 21 in their first game without Harper.

San Antonio outscored New Orleans 82-62 over the final three quarters.

The Spurs captured a 61-45 lead at halftime after two scuffles in the second quarter.

Jaron Pierre Jr. shoved Wembanyama from behind after the 7-foot-4 center was fouled by Karlo Matković with 9:27 remaining in the first half. Technical fouls were given to Pierre and Keldon Johnson , who confronted the Pelicans forward after the shove.

Wembanyama responded by scoring the next seven points, including spinning around Yves Missi for a one-handed slam.

De'Aaron Fox received a technical and had to be separated with 3:49 remaining in the first half after the Spurs guard gave a two-handed shove to Fears following a backcourt violation on the New Orleans guard.

Wembanyama again responded, scoring the next five points.

articles.title: Wembanyama's jab at the NBA stars: Doncic or LeBron?
articles.standfirst: The player said that he doesn’t pad his stats like others do
articles.summary: The player said that he doesn’t pad his stats like others do
articles.body:
After finishing his performance against the Pelicans with 50 points, 19 rebounds, four steals and five blocks , one of the best individual displays of the season, Victor Wembanyama took a swipe courtside at some of the NBA stars accused by some critics of padding their stats. Among the players criticized for that are Luka Doncic, LeBron James , Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Nikola Jokic.

Asked about how special his performance was, the Frenchman said with a mischievous smile: " It's something very special. But, unlike many of my colleagues, I'm not very good at padding stats . That's why I haven't managed to do it as many times as I should have."

And that's despite his coach telling him he had a minute and a half left to reach 50 before being substituted , and the center took two three-pointers, which he made, to achieve it before heading to the bench.

However, when asked again at the press conference, now somewhat calmer after his blunder, Wemby tried to walk back what he said: " The greats don't think about that. I don't think LeBron, Shai, Jokic or Doncic think about that. I look up to them, so I try not to think about it either ," said the Frenchman, downplaying what minutes earlier had seemed like a full-blown dig at one of them.

articles.title: LeBron James refuses to settle and sets the standard that defines 76ers championship mentality
articles.standfirst: The 41-year-old delivered another impressive performance against the Bucks
articles.summary: The 41-year-old delivered another impressive performance against the Bucks
articles.body:
LeBron James has spent more than two decades understanding what separates a talented NBA team from a championship contender, and the Philadelphia 76ers received another reminder of his demanding standards following Saturday's narrow victory over the Milwaukee Bucks .

Philadelphia escaped with a 132-129 win at Xfinity Mobile Arena, extending its winning streak to five games despite requiring a decisive fourth-quarter contribution from James to overcome one of the league's struggling teams.

The 41-year-old scored 13 of his 21 points in the final period, helping Philadelphia preserve a victory that appeared increasingly uncertain as Milwaukee threatened to force overtime.

However, rather than celebrating another successful outing, James acknowledged that the Sixers had allowed their opponents too many opportunities to remain competitive.

“There’s a lot of things we could have done a lot better, but this is professional sports, and it’s hard to win in professional sports,” James said during his postgame interview.

“No matter what league it is. So, we don’t take that for granted. We accept that, for sure, with grace.”

His response reflected the expectations at Philadelphia following his summer arrival from the Los Angeles Lakers , with the franchise now leading the Eastern Conference standings.

The problem Philadelphia 76ers cannot ignore

Despite the final result, Philadelphia struggled to contain a Milwaukee offense inspired by a remarkable performance from Tyler Herro .

The Bucks guard scored a career-high 50 points, adding 11 rebounds and seven assists while making seven three-pointers in an extraordinary individual display.

Milwaukee also held advantages in rebounding, three-point shooting and free-throw accuracy, raising questions about Philadelphia's defensive consistency against a team enduring a difficult campaign.

The contest almost reached overtime when Herro converted what appeared to be a game-tying three-pointer in the closing seconds, only for officials to determine that he released the ball too late.

James finished with six rebounds, six assists, three steals and a block, while Joel Embiid contributed 26 points, 17 rebounds and nine assists.

Nevertheless, the veteran forward made clear that Philadelphia's ambitions extend considerably beyond collecting regular-season victories.

“But understanding, though, what we want to be, what we want to accomplish, we got to be a lot better,” James added.

Barlow explains LeBron influence

While James remains critical of the team's overall execution, his impact on Philadelphia's younger players continues to draw praise.

Dominick Barlow made his long-awaited season debut against Milwaukee after recovering from a back injury, recording 12 points, four rebounds and an assist in just 11 minutes.

The 23-year-old, who hadn't played competitively for nearly 200 days, described how James ' passing and attacking presence make life considerably easier for his teammates.

“He makes my life easy. All we’ve got to do is get the rebound and run. He can throw in the pocket, he can throw in the lob, he can find you in open space,” Barlow said. “The gravity he has driving to the rim is just ridiculous, still at his age.”

Philadelphia's winning streak demonstrates the potential within its roster, but James ' reaction offered a clear reminder that its ultimate ambitions will demand more consistent performances.

articles.title: “Dwight hated Kobe, Kobe hated Dwight”: Howard criticizes media for fabricating Lakers rivalry
articles.standfirst: The former Lakers center has challenged reports of personal feud between the two stars
articles.summary: The former Lakers center has challenged reports of personal feud between the two stars
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers assembled one of the NBA's most formidable-looking rosters in 2012, but their championship ambitions quickly unraveled amid injuries, disappointing results and relentless speculation about the relationship between Kobe Bryant and Dwight Howard .

More than a decade later, Howard is challenging one of the most enduring narratives from that troubled campaign, insisting the apparent personal feud between himself and Bryant was largely manufactured by the media.

Speaking with Casey Kiernan on The AM Hoops Show, the former Lakers center reflected on how their professional disagreements became the subject of widespread reports suggesting that the two superstars genuinely disliked each other.

"I know, the media happened," Howard said when asked about the perception of their relationship. "That's what. The media. Dwight hate Kobe. Kobe hate Dwight. And none of us ever said that, but the media did."

The comments revisit a partnership that promised to transform the Lakers into championship contenders but lasted just one season before Howard departed for the Houston Rockets .

Howard explains controversial Lakers photo

Howard arrived in Los Angeles following a blockbuster trade with the Orlando Magic , joining Bryant, Steve Nash, Pau Gasol and Metta World Peace on a roster carrying enormous expectations.

However, Howard was recovering from back surgery when the season began and subsequently suffered a torn labrum in his right shoulder, creating uncertainty over his availability and physical condition.

Bryant publicly expressed frustration with the team's situation, while reports suggested that the two players disagreed about Howard 's willingness to compete through injuries.

"People were saying Kobe should have been my doctor when I got hurt. And I should have went to him and told him about my injuries instead of telling the actual doctors. Which didn't make any sense to me," Howard explained.

Speculation intensified in January 2013 following reports that the teammates had nearly confronted each other after a disappointing defeat against Philadelphia.

Bryant responded by posting a photograph showing himself and Howard adopting boxing poses, accompanied by the caption: "The mamba vs d12 !! It's on lol".

Howard insists the picture was intended to demonstrate that their relationship was not as hostile as reports suggested.

"That was a picture to show that we cool like we ain't got no beef. But then they took it as that," he said.

Howard admits regret over Lakers exit

The Lakers eventually finished the regular season with a 45-37 record before suffering a first-round playoff sweep against the San Antonio Spurs after Bryant sustained a torn Achilles tendon.

Howard subsequently signed a four-year, $88 million contract with Houston, a decision he now acknowledges was influenced by his emotions.

"At the time of making decisions, if your emotions are so high, you won't be able to see the big picture," Howard said. "Yes, I think it was an emotional decision instead of looking long-term."

Nevertheless, Howard also identified basketball and financial considerations, including the opportunity to learn from Hakeem Olajuwon and Kevin McHale while playing alongside James Harden .

His NBA career eventually brought him back to Los Angeles in 2019, when he helped the Lakers win the 2020 championship.

Although their original partnership failed to meet expectations, Howard 's latest comments suggest that the public perception of his relationship with Bryant never reflected the complete story.

articles.title: Is Wemby trying to impress? Victor Wembanyama jokingly admits that he “had to show off” with Selena Gomez in the stands
articles.standfirst: The 22-year-old produced another extraordinary NBA performance
articles.summary: The 22-year-old produced another extraordinary NBA performance
articles.body:
A sold-out crowd at Frost Bank Center witnessed another remarkable performance from Victor Wembanyama on Saturday night, but the San Antonio Spurs star admitted that one particular spectator had given him an extra reason to put on a show.

Selena Gomez was sitting courtside as Wembanyama produced one of the most extraordinary statistical performances of his young NBA career, leading San Antonio to a commanding 114-91 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans .

The 22-year-old Frenchman finished with 50 points, 18 rebounds, five blocks and four steals in just 32 minutes, reinforcing his reputation as one of the league's most dominant players.

However, it was his reaction to a successful three-pointer that generated an unexpected talking point after the game.

Wembanyama appeared to glance toward the crowd following the shot, prompting a reporter to ask whether he had been acknowledging someone in attendance.

"Of course I had to show off for Selena, you know," Wembanyama replied with a smile, drawing laughter from reporters.

His lighthearted admission provided a memorable conclusion to an evening that had already established another significant milestone in his rapidly developing career.

Victor Wembanyama makes NBA history with Selena Gomez watching courtside

Wembanyama's performance was remarkable from the opening half, when he accumulated 32 points, 13 rebounds, three blocks and three steals to help San Antonio establish a 61-45 advantage.

The Spurs center eventually converted 20 of his 29 field-goal attempts, including five three-pointers, while making five of six free throws.

His combination of scoring, rebounding and defensive contributions made him the first player in NBA history to record at least 50 points, 18 rebounds, five blocks, four steals and five three-pointers in a single game.

New Orleans attempted to disrupt his rhythm through physical defense, with several confrontations resulting in technical fouls during the opening half.

Wembanyama remained largely unaffected, responding with another impressive scoring sequence that included a powerful one-handed dunk against Yves Missi .

The victory improved San Antonio's record to 14-3, keeping the Spurs level with the Los Angeles Lakers near the top of the Western Conference standings.

Spurs superstar explains his unusual comments about stat padding

Beyond his exchange about Gomez , Wembanyama attracted attention with another playful remark concerning the pursuit of individual scoring milestones.

"It is very special. Unlike many of my peers, I'm not very good at stat padding," he said during his on-court interview.

The Frenchman subsequently clarified his comments, explaining that he looks toward established NBA stars when deciding how aggressively to pursue scoring opportunities.

"But the greats, they don't think about that. I don't think LeBron, Shai, Jokic, Doncic think about that. And I have them as examples. So I try not to think about it either," he explained.

Wembanyama also revealed that coach Mitch Johnson had given him a final opportunity to reach 50 points before withdrawing him from the game.

"(Johnson) did tell me that at some point I had 1:30 left of play time and he said he wished I had come to 50, but I only have 1:30 left and I told him it might be enough," Wembanyama recalled.

The achievement marked his second 50-point performance of November, with Stephon Castle contributing another 19 points and six assists in the victory.

While the numbers demonstrated Wembanyama's growing influence on the court, his joking acknowledgment of Gomez revealed a more relaxed side to the young superstar following another historic performance.

articles.title: LeBron James has a special message from his “nephew” for the Bucks point guard who grew up playing with Bryce James
articles.standfirst: After rookie guard Brayden Burries erupted for a career-high 26 points off the bench in Philadelphia, the 76ers superstar celebrated a full-circle moment with a former Strive for Greatness standout he has mentored since childhood
articles.summary: After rookie guard Brayden Burries erupted for a career-high 26 points off the bench in Philadelphia, the 76ers superstar celebrated a full-circle moment with a former Strive for Greatness standout he has mentored since childhood
articles.body:
Over more than two decades in the NBA , LeBron James has shared the hardwood with the sons of former rivals, squared off against players raised idolizing him, and prepared for matchups against his own eldest son, Bronny James .

On Saturday afternoon in Philadelphia, however, the new Philadelphia 76ers forward experienced a deeply personal milestone of a different kind, facing off against Brayden Burries , a 21-year-old Milwaukee Bucks rookie whom James has coached, mentored, and treated like family for more than a decade.

Inside Xfinity Mobile Arena, Eastern Conference-leading Philadelphia (14-3) narrowly survived a furious fourth-quarter push from Milwaukee (1-16) to claim a 132-129 victory.

Bucks guard Tyler Herro commanded plenty of headlines with a career-high 50-point explosion, and nearly forced overtime before officials ruled his final right-wing three-pointer left his fingertips just after the buzzer, prompting 76ers center Joel Embiid to reportedly praise Herro as a “top-five player in the league.”

Yet amid the late-game drama, James’s focus quickly turned to Burries, who poured in a career-best 26 points, including a clutch corner three with 4.8 seconds left that briefly pulled Milwaukee within a single point.

Shortly after the final horn, the official NBA social media account captured the postgame embrace between veteran and rookie, posting: “@braydenburries0 embraced his former AAU coach, @kingjames, after they faced each other today in Philly! 🙌.”

James soon reposted the clip to his Instagram Story with an emotional tribute to the young guard he affectionately calls family: “So proud of him!! so so so proud! Keep going nephew 🙏🏻🫡🫶.”

From youth AAU courts and Arizona to facing off on an NBA floor

The bond between James and Burries stretches back long before either imagined sharing an NBA court.

Burries first connected with the James family when he was roughly eight years old, eventually rising through the ranks on the Nike EYBL circuit with James’s Strive for Greatness AAU program. Playing alongside LeBron’s youngest son, Bryce James , Burries developed into a premier prospect before carrying that friendship to the college level at the University of Arizona.

In fact, Bryce played a direct role in steering Burries toward Tucson as part of the Wildcats’ highly touted recruiting class. Recalling how his longtime teammate recruited him to join the program, Burries explained that Bryce reached out with a simple pitch: “Yo, come to Arizona.”

The two remained close throughout their time together with the Wildcats, and when Milwaukee selected Burries with the 10th overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Bryce celebrated the milestone on Instagram by posting “Prada u boy” accompanied by four red hearts.

Entering the league with lottery-pick expectations, Burries has provided a bright spot during an otherwise difficult opening month for the Bucks. Across his first 16 appearances prior to Saturday’s matinee, he averaged 10.4 points, 5.3 rebounds, and 2.3 assists.

Even after shifting back to a reserve role against Philadelphia following a 10-game stretch as a starter, the rookie showcased the poise, rebounding, and scoring punch that boosted his 17-game season averages to approximately 11.3 points, 5.5 rebounds, and 2.4 assists per contest, guided by a foundational piece of advice James gave him years ago: “Just be you, go out there and compete, have fun, play hard.”

Of course, the 22-time All-Star made sure his former pupil did not leave Philadelphia with a victory. James stuffed the box score with 21 points, six rebounds, six assists, and three steals on 9-of-14 shooting in 35 minutes of action.

He sparked a 38-33 third-quarter turnaround by throwing down an emphatic dunk, rejecting a Kyle Kuzma shot, and feeding Tyrese Maxey for a go-ahead basket, before pouring in 13 of his 21 points during the fourth quarter to seal the win for Philadelphia, turning a hard-fought Eastern Conference battle into an unforgettable afternoon for mentor and protégé alike.

articles.title: The giant Walker Kessler who is as crucial for the Lakers as Doncic: "It may sound like blasphemy..."
articles.standfirst: Center Walker Kessler is having a major impact on the Lakers' strong performance, led by Luka Doncic, at the start of the season
articles.summary: Center Walker Kessler is having a major impact on the Lakers' strong performance, led by Luka Doncic, at the start of the season
articles.body:
At Sports Illustrated they believe that Walker Kessler , the giant engaged to Miss America , is as important as Luka Doncic to the Lakers .

Chris Mannix and Evan Turner analyze the impact of the giant Walker Kessler (2.18 m and 111 kg) on the Los Angeles Lakers' game, especially his incredible defensive performance and the balance he creates on offense (he has a special connection with Doncic when running "pick-and-rolls" (screen-and-rolls)).

It is possible to win an NBA championship with a middling defense, so the reality is that they depend as much on Kessler on defense as they do on Doncic on offense

"It may sound like blasphemy, but who do they have who is capable of taking on Kessler’s role: grabbing rebounds, blocking shots, and cleaning things up on defense?" they ask.

Chris Mannix and Evan Turner believe that the Lakers "have a fairly narrow margin for error" and that "it is possible to win an NBA championship with an average-level defense, as Denver showed three or four years ago, so the reality is that they depend as much on Kessler on defense as on Doncic on offense".

For the Lakers to succeed, they need Kessler to play, more or less, around 70 games... He is one of the 15 best defensive players in the NBA and a fundamental piece of the system

"For the Lakers to succeed, they need Kessler, who missed most of the 2025-26 season because of a shoulder injury, to play roughly around 70 games... He is one of the 15 best defensive players in the NBA and a fundamental piece of the system," they concluded about the center, who arrived in Los Angeles from the Utah Jazz in exchange for two future first-round Draft picks and two future first-round pick swap rights.

Rob Pelinka already warned it: "At the core of every great Lakers team there is a dominant big man"

Rob Pelinka, president of basketball operations and general manager of the Los Angeles Lakers, already warned after signing Kessler that "at the core of every great Lakers team there is a dominant big man."

Since his NBA debut in the 2022-23 season, only Victor Wembanyama has averaged more blocks per game than Kessler.

The statistics confirm Walker Kessler's impact on Doncic's Lakers

Walker Kessler, who signed with the Lakers for $130 million over four years , is averaging 14.3 points (he leads the NBA with a 66.4% field-goal percentage), 10.7 rebounds, and 2.1 blocks in 30.9 minutes.

With Kessler on the court, the Lakers allow only 111.0 points per 100 possessions and reduce opponents' shooting accuracy near the rim by nearly 13%. Advanced metrics from "Cleaning the Glass" highlight that the center has the third-best On/Off differential on the entire roster (+7.3 Plus/Minus per game), behind only Doncic and Austin Reaves.

One of his weak points is his accuracy from the free-throw line, where he makes only 59.7% of his shots.

articles.title: With Kevon Looney out of rotation, here’s the exact trade the Lakers need to back up Walker Kessler
articles.standfirst: With Kessler excelling and the backup center position unsettled, a former All-Star could provide the offensive versatility needed
articles.summary: With Kessler excelling and the backup center position unsettled, a former All-Star could provide the offensive versatility needed
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers have enjoyed an outstanding start to the NBA season, but their impressive 14-3 record has done little to disguise a growing concern about the depth of their frontcourt.

Walker Kessler has established himself as a valuable addition alongside Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves , providing the rebounding and interior protection that Los Angeles desperately needed.

However, the Lakers have struggled to find a reliable replacement whenever their starting center leaves the floor, with veteran Kevon Looney increasingly finding himself outside JJ Redick 's preferred rotation.

Looney has appeared in just seven games, averaging 7.3 minutes, despite arriving with considerable championship experience from his years with the Golden State Warriors .

Redick has instead relied on Jarred Vanderbilt in smaller lineups, sacrificing offensive versatility to maintain defensive intensity when Kessler rests.

According to NBA insider Marc Stein , Los Angeles is exploring the market for another center, with the approaching trade window potentially offering an opportunity to address the imbalance.

One player worth considering is Orlando Magic veteran Nikola Vucevic , whose reduced role this season could make him an intriguing option.

Vucevic has endured a frustrating start to the campaign, averaging just 3.7 points in limited minutes after signing a one-year, $3.9 million contract with Orlando.

However, his offensive capabilities remain considerably more developed than those of the Lakers ' current reserve big men.

The 36-year-old averaged 16.9 points, nine rebounds and 3.8 assists during his final season with the Chicago Bulls before joining the Boston Celtics .

His ability to score from the post, distribute the ball and stretch opposing defenses would provide Redick with a different option behind Kessler .

That distinction could become particularly valuable given how heavily Los Angeles depends on Doncic , who is averaging more than 38 points per game, to generate offensive opportunities.

Kessler has been outstanding himself, contributing 14.3 points, 10.7 rebounds and 2.1 blocks while shooting an NBA-leading 66.4 percent from the field.

The center recently demonstrated his developing perimeter confidence by making a three-pointer against Sacramento.

"It was open," Kessler explained afterward. "I'm confident in that shot. It was open, and Bull [Collin Sexton] actually told me to space."

The trade Lakers should consider

Los Angeles could explore offering Looney and a future second-round draft pick to Orlando in exchange for Vucevic , creating a relatively inexpensive route toward greater offensive depth.

Such a proposal would depend on salary-matching requirements, trade eligibility and the Magic 's willingness to part with their veteran center.

Vucevic wouldn't provide the same rim protection as Kessler , and his defensive limitations could become problematic against quicker opponents.

However, pairing him with Vanderbilt could help compensate for those weaknesses while allowing the Lakers to maintain a more balanced second unit.

The proposed exchange would also preserve Los Angeles' more valuable draft assets, leaving the front office flexibility to pursue additional reinforcements.

With Doncic operating at an exceptional level and Kessler proving his value, the Lakers already possess the foundations of a serious championship contender.

Adding a proven offensive center on an affordable contract could provide the additional versatility needed when the postseason arrives.

articles.title: Warriors could make blockbuster move for Anthony Davis as championship window begins to close
articles.standfirst: Golden State's inconsistent start has raised questions about whether its current roster is good enough to compete with the Western Conference’s best
articles.summary: Golden State's inconsistent start has raised questions about whether its current roster is good enough to compete with the Western Conference’s best
articles.body:
T he Golden State Warriors may have reached a point where standing pat is no longer an option. With S tephen Curry and the franchise’s championship ambitions still at the center of the organization, the front office could consider an aggressive move to bring Anthony Davis to the Bay Area.

Davis , who currently plays for the Washington Wizards , recently earned Eastern Conference Player of the Week honors for Week 5 of the 2026-27 NBA season (Nov. 16-22), further demonstrating that he remains one of the league’s most impactful big men.

The former Los Angeles Lakers star, who won an NBA championship alongside LeBron James in 2020, could offer precisely what Golden State needs: interior defense, rebounding, and another elite scoring option capable of taking pressure off Curry.

The Warriors have endured a difficult stretch, losing five consecutive games before snapping the skid with a victory over the Boston Celtics. That win moved Golden State to 9-8, but the team’s inconsistent start has raised questions about whether its current roster is good enough to compete with the Western Conference’s best.

A potential Davis acquisition would be an enormous gamble, but it could also represent the kind of move that changes the Warriors’ season.

The trade package that could bring Davis to Golden State

Acquiring a player of Davis’ caliber would not come cheaply. The Warriors would likely need to make difficult decisions involving some of their most important veterans and valuable future assets.

One proposed trade scenario would send the following package to Washington : Draymond Green and Moses Moody, draft compensation, protected 2031 first-round pick (top-three protection), 2030 second-round pick, and 2033 second-round pick.

From Washington’s perspective , the appeal would be getting younger, accumulating draft capital and creating additional flexibility for its rebuilding project. The Wizards are building around young talent, including AJ Dybantsa, and could benefit from moving a veteran whose long-term future with the organization remains uncertain.

Green would provide an experienced player and potentially significant contract flexibility, depending on his respective contract structures. Moody, meanwhile, would give Washington a younger wing who could become part of its longer-term plans.

The draft picks could become particularly valuable as Golden State’s current championship core eventually moves toward the end of its competitive window.

However, the proposed package would require careful salary-cap and trade-rule calculations. The players’ contracts, trade eligibility and Washington’s willingness to accept the assets would all need to be evaluated before such a deal could become realistic.

Why Anthony Davis would be an ideal fit for the Warriors

The basketball argument for bringing D avis to Golden State is compelling, particularly because of the team’s problems protecting the paint and generating consistent offense without Curry. The 10-time All-Star remains one of the NBA’s most versatile big men . His ability to defend multiple positions, protect the rim, rebound and score from different areas of the floor would address several of Golden State’s biggest weaknesses.

His recent Player of the Week performance provided another reminder of what he can bring to a contender. During the week of Nov. 16-22, Davis averaged: 26.5 points, nine rebounds, 1.3 blocks and 58.6% field-goal percentage per game.

Davis helped Washington win three of its four games during that stretch, recording 36 points and 11 rebounds against Chicago and 25 points with 14 rebounds against Toronto . His 22-point performance against Orlando helped the Wizards secure another victory. It was his 12th career Player of the Week award and his first since October 2024, when he was playing for the Lakers.

For the season, Davis is averaging 25.1 points, 9.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.2 blocks and 1.1 steals per game, according to the Wizards’ announcement. Those numbers would make him an enormous addition to a Golden State team searching for a reliable interior presence.

Davis could also become the Warriors’ primary offensive option whenever Curry needs a break or faces defensive pressure. His ability to operate in the post, finish around the basket and knock down midrange shots would give Steve Kerr another way to generate offense.

Defensively, the potential impact might be even greater. Golden State would have a proven rim protector capable of changing opponents’ decisions around the basket, while also improving its rebounding and transition defense.

The prospect of pairing Davis with Curry, Jimmy Butler and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg would make Golden State considerably more dangerous when its key players are available.

The risks: Davis’ health and an expensive contract

Despite the obvious basketball benefits, trading for Davis would carry considerable financial and medical risks. His injury history has been a recurring concern throughout his career. Although he has remained productive during the current season, the Warriors would need to carefully evaluate whether he could maintain that availability over a full season and a deep playoff run.

There is also the financial commitment. Davis reportedly has a $62.8 million player option for the 2027-28 season, a substantial figure that could complicate Golden State’s roster-building plans . If he exercises that option, the Warriors would be committing an enormous portion of their financial resources to a player entering the later stages of his career.

Giving up Green would also be an emotionally significant decision. The veteran forward has been central to Golden State’s championship identity, providing defensive leadership, playmaking and an intensity that cannot easily be replaced. His partnership with Curry has helped define one of the most successful eras in NBA history.

articles.summary: The court documents from the James family's complaints against the two men who broke into their home thinking they were members of their family are leaked
articles.body:
Savannah, LeBron James' wife , reveals terrifying details about the intrusions of two alleged stalkers into her Los Angeles mansion (United States) that recall the Oscar-winning film "Parasite" (in which a family infiltrates the home of a wealthy family).

My family is safe and that's the most important thing. We are still investigating everything that happened

articles.title: Stephen Curry’s injury pushes the Warriors to hunt for All-Star help on the trade market
articles.standfirst: Curry doesn't have a return date yet, and it likely won't be until just before Christmas
articles.summary: Curry doesn't have a return date yet, and it likely won't be until just before Christmas
articles.body:
Few franchises in the NBA rely as heavily on a single superstar as the Golden State Warriors , who look like two completely different teams with and without Stephen Curry on the floor.

After roaring out to an 8-3 record while Curry averaged 30.6 points per game on 45.7 percent shooting from deep , Golden State saw its momentum stall when the two-time MVP exited the November 11 clash against the Houston Rockets in the opening quarter with right abdominal soreness.

Since that night, the Warriors have stumbled to a 1-5 mark , dropping to 9-8 overall. Although an MRI confirmed an oblique tear , the franchise has yet to specify whether Curry is dealing with a Grade 1 oblique strain, which typically carries a two-to-four-week recovery window, or a more severe Grade 2 injury that can sideline a player for three to eight weeks.

In the meantime, the front office must figure out how to stay afloat in a crowded Western Conference and seriously weigh external reinforcements on the NBA trade market .

Franz Wagner, and Bargain Targets Lead Warriors’ Trade Market Options

Golden State is widely expected to dangle Kristaps Porzingis ’ expiring contract as a salary-matching chip once the December 16 trade restriction lifts, allowing the club to stay aggressive ahead of the February 11 deadline .

If the Warriors prefer chasing a younger cornerstone, O rlando Magic forward Franz Wagner stands out as a premier two-way needle-mover under contract through at least 2028-29.

Acquiring the 25-year-old wing, and absorbing his $41.8 million salary , would likely demand a steep haul of three first-round draft picks in addition to Porzingis, yet Wagner’s size and playmaking would instantly elevate Golden State’s ceiling alongside Curry.

For a far cheaper route that preserves future draft assets, Golden State could pivot toward bargain-bin veterans in Milwaukee , where center Myles Turner and forward Kyle Kuzma have both landed on the trade radar.

Turner is enduring the lowest-producing season of his career, which has pushed his market value down to roughly a single second-round pick , while Kuzma offers inexpensive frontcourt scoring depth on an expiring deal that wouldn’t force the Warriors to gut their roster.

Regardless of which path general manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. pursues, internal help is also slowly approaching: Jimmy Butler continues progressing in his rehab from the torn ACL he suffered back in January 2026, with the veteran forward targeting a return to the lineup right around All-Star Weekend in February.

If Golden State can survive Curry’s current absence, pull off a smart midseason trade, and welcome a healthy Butler back for the stretch run, the Warriors could still transform into a dangerous postseason threat.

articles.title: How a Michael Jordan retirement rumor changed Kobe Bryant’s entire NBA career
articles.standfirst: A former NBA star has revealed how concerns about Jordan’s potential retirement helped shape Bryant’s path to the NBA
articles.summary: A former NBA star has revealed how concerns about Jordan’s potential retirement helped shape Bryant’s path to the NBA
articles.body:
A resurfaced story about Kobe Bryant’s decision to enter the NBA straight out of high school has provide a fascinating explanation as to why the youngster was so keen to join the league.

It turns out Bryant believed Michael Jordan might retire, and he didn’t want to miss the opportunity to compete against his childhood idol.

Former NBA player John Salley shared the anecdote during a 2024 appearance on Byron Scott’s “Fast Break” podcast. Salley recalled asking Bryant why he hadn’t attended college before declaring for the NBA Draft.

“I said to him, ‘Why’d you not go to college?’ And he says, ‘I heard MJ was going to retire,’” Salley said. “And that was his reason for not going to college.”

That decision helped shape Bryant’s remarkable career. At just 17, he entered the 1996 NBA Draft, where the Charlotte Hornets selected him 13th overall before trading him to the Los Angeles Lakers.

Jordan , meanwhile, continued playing for the Chicago Bulls through 1998, eventually retiring for a second time before returning with the Washington Wizards in 2001. His playing career finally ended in 2003.

Bryant ultimately got the opportunity he’d hoped for. The two superstars faced each other eight times during the regular season, with Bryant’s teams winning five matchups.

Although they never met in the playoffs, their encounters created a fascinating connection between two generations of basketball greatness.

Jordan’s influence continued through Kobe Bryant’s legacy

The connection between the legendary guards has resurfaced as another NBA superstar has spoken about Bryant’s lasting influence.

James Harden recently moved past Bryant into third place on the league’s all-time list of 50-point games, recording his 26th career performance with a 51-point effort for the Cleveland Cavaliers against Indiana on November 20.

Harden was quick to acknowledge what reaching the milestone meant, particularly because Bryant had been such an important figure during his childhood.

“My idol,” Harden said of Bryant . “The person I watched growing up. The way he cared about the game and effort he put in is something special. We miss him and miss him a lot.”

Bryant finished his career with 25 50-point performances, while Jordan recorded 31. Wilt Chamberlain remains comfortably ahead with 118.

Despite sharing an extraordinary ability to score, Bryant and Harden developed very different offensive approaches. Bryant became famous for his footwork, difficult mid-range jumpers and ability to create shots under pressure, particularly during important moments.

Harden , meanwhile, combines isolation scoring with his playmaking and three-point shooting. He averages 7.6 three-point attempts per game throughout his career, compared with Bryant’s 4.1.

Their relationship also included some honest basketball disagreements. Bryant questioned in 2019 whether Harden’s heavily isolation-based approach could produce an NBA championship, although he acknowledged the importance of Harden carrying his team offensively.

Bryant retired with five championships, two Finals MVP awards, an NBA MVP and 18 All-Star selections. Harden has built an impressive résumé of his own, including 11 All-Star appearances, eight All-NBA selections, three scoring titles and a Sixth Man of the Year award.

articles.title: Jalen Brunson ‘can’t believe’ he has to defend Taylor Swift’s fandom after teammate’s diss
articles.standfirst: The Knicks captain makes his feelings clear as controversy over Swift's team loyalty continues
articles.summary: The Knicks captain makes his feelings clear as controversy over Swift's team loyalty continues
articles.body:
New York Knicks captain Jalen Brunson has found himself in an unexpected position: defending Taylor Swift’s credentials as a genuine supporter of the team after a teammate questioned her loyalty.

The NBA star addressed the growing controversy after Tyler Kolek suggested that the pop superstar’s connection to the Knicks was more about appearances than actual support.

Speaking to Us Weekly, Brunson made it clear that Swift is welcome at Madison Square Garden and deserves recognition as part of the team's fan base.

“I can’t believe I have to say this,” he said. “But I didn’t say what was said. Being one of the leaders of the team — the captain of the team — I guess I now have to help somebody out. Yes, she’s a member of the Knicks fandom. Yes, she is.”

The disagreement dates back to the 2026 NBA playoffs. Swift attended Game 3 of the Eastern Conference finals in Cleveland alongside her husband, Travis Kelce , who was supporting his hometown Cavaliers.

Although New York eventually swept Cleveland, her appearance at the opposing team's game raised questions about where her basketball loyalties actually stood.

Swift later made her presence felt at Madison Square Garden during Game 4 of the NBA Finals in June.

Sitting courtside with friends Mariska Hargitay and sisters Alana and Este Haim, she wore a blue “Stevie Knicks” shirt and celebrated as New York produced a stunning 29-point comeback, capped by OG Anunoby's decisive game-winning tip-in.

Tyler Kolek’s comments reignite the debate

The discussion resurfaced in November when Tyler Kolek was asked during an NBA 2K TikTok livestream to identify the most inauthentic celebrity Knicks supporter.

He suggested Swift's appearances were “performative”, arguing that he hadn't seen her attend many other games and questioning whether certain celebrities were more interested in being noticed than supporting the team.

“Maybe Taylor Swift ? I don’t know if I’ve seen her at any other games,” he added. “I guess she has a lot going on so she can’t come all the time. But it’s a little performative.”

His comments quickly attracted criticism from Swift's devoted fan base. Some supporters highlighted Kolek's limited playing time during the Finals, drawing comparisons between his court appearances and Swift's courtside presence.

The Knicks organisation later issued a statement defending the singer, confirming that she'd supported the franchise for years and maintained a longstanding connection with Madison Square Garden.

" Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization," the statement read.

Kolek later apologized, admitting that he might have handled the question poorly. He also insisted that he had nothing against Swift , revealing that he enjoyed her music and had recently been singing along to her songs with teammates.

Brunson's comments adds further weight to the team's defense. Swift's association with Madison Square Garden also extends beyond basketball, as she and Kelce celebrated their wedding there on July 3.

Meanwhile, the defending champions have plenty to concentrate on on the court. New York enter Wednesday's meeting with Cleveland at 11-6, riding a five-game winning streak after defeating Indiana 113-106. The Heat and Hawks are also scheduled during the Thanksgiving weekend.

articles.title: Shaquille O’Neal prepared himself for the possibility of losing his fortune with a 75-25 money rule
articles.standfirst: A wealthy man’s napkin advice led Shaq to save most of his endorsement money and buy annuities
articles.summary: A wealthy man’s napkin advice led Shaq to save most of his endorsement money and buy annuities
articles.body:
Shaquille O’Neal says he didn’t want his financial future to depend on every investment working out. The idea that helped him prepare for that possibility came from a wealthy man, a napkin and a simple split: spend 25% of your money and save 75%.

O’Neal says he followed that advice with endorsement checks and put a large portion into annuities as a backup plan.

The math is straightforward: for every $100, set aside $75 and use the remaining $25 for spending . It reverses the familiar idea of saving half and spending half. O’Neal recalled the advice during a episode of the Dinner Party podcast, saying the man told him that saving three-quarters was the way to build wealth.

The rule is best understood as a budgeting principle, not a formal financial formula with a documented origin. Its broader idea save before spending and keep lifestyle costs below income also appears in mainstream financial guidance.

O’Neal had shared a similar version years earlier : in a 2017 interview, he advised young NBA players to save 75% of their earnings and use the other 25% as they wished.

That doesn’t mean the same percentage works for everyone. Shaq was talking about high NBA and endorsement income; for a household with rent, debt and other essential costs, saving 75% may be unrealistic.

His story illustrates what the rule did for him, but there’s no public record showing how much he saved under it or proving that the rule alone produced his wealth.

Why Shaq wanted a financial safety net

O’Neal said he began setting aside endorsement checks after hearing the advice. As money accumulated, he invested in businesses, but wanted a source of income in case those investments failed. “That was my fail-proof” plan, he said on the podcast.

He said the annuities are scheduled to pay him at ages 55, 60 and 65. O’Neal turns 55 in March 2027 and estimated that he could receive about $1 million a month at that age. He has not disclosed the premiums, insurers or contract terms behind that estimate, so the figure remains his own projection not a publicly verified payout.

An annuity is a contract with an insurance company: a person pays a lump sum or a series of payments, and the insurer agrees to provide income immediately or at a future date, depending on the contract.

Some annuities can provide payments for life, but the details vary. Early withdrawals may bring surrender charges and tax consequences, and the insurer’s ability to pay matters.

O’Neal’s plan comes as Americans are buying more annuities. LIMRA reported that U.S. sales reached a record $126.3 billion in the third quarter of 2026, up 4% from a year earlier.

That total covers different kinds of annuities, however; it doesn’t mean every buyer is purchasing a product that guarantees lifetime income.

O’Neal’s financial story is still unfolding alongside his business ventures. In 2026, he launched DUNKMAN , a professional dunk league with TNT Sports and Authentic Brands Group; Eli Lilly joined as a partner.

The league gives him another business to grow while the annuities he describes are meant to provide a separate source of future income.

articles.title: Stephen Curry puts his Warriors worries behind him and enjoys himself at Cameron Brink's spectacular wedding with Ayesha
articles.standfirst: The four-time NBA champion traded basketball stress for family celebration as his god-sister married longtime partner Ben Felter in Northern California
articles.summary: The four-time NBA champion traded basketball stress for family celebration as his god-sister married longtime partner Ben Felter in Northern California
articles.body:
Dealing with an oblique tear while watching the Golden State Warriors stumble through a winless road trip would test any superstar’s patience, yet Stephen Curry found the ideal escape from NBA frustration earlier this month.

On November 14, Curry and his wife, Ayesha , dressed to the nines to celebrate the wedding of Los Angeles Sparks forward Cameron Brink and former Stanford rower Ben Felter , an intimate, picturesque Northern California affair officially unveiled by Vogue on Tuesday, November 24.

The Curry family’s presence carried deep personal significance. Curry’s mother, Sonya , is Brink’s godmother and close best friend of Brink’s mother, Michelle Bain-Brink , meaning Steph grew up alongside the 24-year-old WNBA standout like an older brother.

That lifelong bond was woven throughout the celebration: Ayesha served among Brink’s bridesmaids, Sonya prayed over the couple during the ceremony, and Steph and Ayesha’s daughter, Ryan, acted as flower girl before performing “Until I Found You” during the newlyweds’ first dance.

Smiling broadly in a classic black tuxedo alongside Ayesha , Steph posed for warm group portraits with the bride and groom, temporarily setting aside the headaches of a 9-8 Warriors campaign that has faltered badly during his injury absence.

articles.title: LeBron James' lifestyle that has made him a millionaire: “Only thing I do for free is wake up”
articles.standfirst: A phrase uttered during a golf game went viral and reflects the mindset with which the player built an estimated $1.4 billion fortune. His businesses, investments, and advertising deals explain how he multiplied his income beyond the NBA.
articles.summary: A phrase uttered during a golf game went viral and reflects the mindset with which the player built an estimated $1.4 billion fortune. His businesses, investments, and advertising deals explain how he multiplied his income beyond the NBA.
articles.body:
LeBron James dropped a line that sums up his way of understanding business quite well. During a round of golf in California, the Philadelphia 76ers player joked about the possibility of betting money and made a comment that quickly began circulating on social media: “The only thing I do for free is wake up. After that, it's time to get paid.”

The phrase came up during a conversation with the team from the Dink Cart program at the Spanish Hills Club. What began as a joke in the middle of a golf challenge ended up becoming a viral statement about the entrepreneurial mindset of one of the athletes who has best known how to capitalize on his image and career to generate income.

From Akron to becoming an NBA legend

Born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, LeBron was selected by the Cleveland Cavaliers with the first overall pick in the 2003 Draft . Since then, he built a career that also led him to play for the Miami Heat and the Los Angeles Lakers, before beginning a new chapter in Philadelphia during the 2026-27 season.

Along the way, he won four NBA championship rings , four regular-season MVP awards, and another four as the most valuable player of the Finals. He also became the all-time leading scorer in the competition , a record that cemented his position among basketball’s greatest figures.

How much is LeBron James' fortune worth?

His success on the courts was the starting point for a much broader business. According to an estimate published by Forbes on November 24, 2026, James's net worth reaches approximately $1.4 billion . In this way, he became the first active NBA player to reach that fortune.

An important part of his income comes from commercial deals with companies such as Nike, Amazon, and Fanatics. Added to that are his investments, business stakes, and projects linked to entertainment and audiovisual production.

Instead of simply charging to lend his image, James also sought to take part in the businesses that support his personal brand.

His new chapter in Philadelphia and a very different contract

At 41 years old, LeBron faces the 2026-27 season with the Philadelphia 76ers. After earning $52.6 million in his final campaign with the Lakers, he accepted a two-year contract for approximately eight million with his new team, a considerable difference compared with his previous salary earnings.

In sporting terms, his first games with Philadelphia also produced standout performances. Against Portland he scored 23 points; against Milwaukee he finished with 21 points, six rebounds and six assists, while against Indiana he posted 15 points and 11 assists. Through his first 14 games of the season, he is averaging 16.6 points, 6.7 rebounds and 6.5 assists.

The phrase he uttered during that golf game may have been a joke, but it reflects a side of LeBron that he developed over more than two decades: his ability to turn his sporting success into business opportunities .

articles.title: Knicks star Jalen Brunson clears up teammate blunder with Taylor Swift: “I guess I have to give someone a hand”
articles.standfirst: Tyler Kolek questioned the authenticity of the singer's support for New York
articles.summary: Tyler Kolek questioned the authenticity of the singer's support for New York
articles.body:
Questioning Taylor Swift 's loyalty to the New York Knicks proved to be a risky decision for Tyler Kolek , whose recent comments generated enough controversy to leave team captain Jalen Brunson taking on the unexpected responsibility of defending one of the franchise's most recognizable celebrity supporters.

Kolek found himself at the center of a social media storm earlier this month after identifying Swift as the team's least authentic celebrity fan during an appearance on the NBA's Deflected show.

The remarks prompted Swift 's supporters to produce evidence of her attending Knicks games long before the franchise's recent championship success, forcing Kolek to acknowledge that he was unfamiliar with the singer's history at Madison Square Garden.

Brunson subsequently addressed the situation during an interview with Us Weekly, expressing his amusement at having to intervene in a controversy that had little to do with basketball.

“I can't believe I have to say this. But I didn't say what was said. Being one of the leaders of the team, the captain of the team, I guess I now have to help somebody out,” Brunson said. “Yes, she's a member of the Knicks fandom. Yes, she is.”

Tyler Kolek acknowledges Swift mistake

Although Swift 's appearances during the Knicks ' championship run attracted considerable attention, her association with the franchise stretches back more than a decade. The singer attended games alongside model Karlie Kloss in 2014, when Carmelo Anthony was New York's leading star.

Kolek admitted that supporters had brought those appearances to his attention following his controversial remarks, while insisting that he had nothing against Swift personally.

“It's just a question that was asked of me, that maybe I answered in the wrong way. Take that on the chin,” Kolek told The Athletic. “I love her music. We were just playing it five minutes ago, and I'm singing every word to every song. Nothing against her at all.”

The guard ultimately accepted responsibility for overlooking Swift 's longstanding connection to the franchise, admitting that his knowledge of her basketball allegiances had been somewhat limited.

“That's on me. I wasn't up to date on my Taylor Swift Knicks fandom. So that's on me,” he added.

Taylor Swift's longstanding support

Swift was among the celebrities in attendance when the Knicks produced a memorable comeback against the San Antonio Spurs in Game 4 of the 2026 NBA Finals, helping New York establish a 3-1 series advantage.

Following Kolek 's comments, the organization also took the unusual step of issuing a statement recognizing the singer's relationship with the team.

“Taylor Swift has been a Knicks fan for many years, has a long history with Madison Square Garden, and we are incredibly appreciative of her support of the organization,” the Knicks said.

Away from the controversy, Kolek has been enjoying an encouraging season, averaging a career-high 4.1 assists while helping the Knicks establish a five-game winning streak.

His performances have given supporters plenty of reasons to focus on basketball again, while Brunson 's intervention has left little doubt about where the franchise stands on Swift 's place among the Knicks faithful.

articles.title: Luka is on track to achieve something with the Lakers not even Kobe or LeBron were able to
articles.standfirst: The Slovenian superstar can use his size to protect the ball, create space and shoot over defenders
articles.summary: The Slovenian superstar can use his size to protect the ball, create space and shoot over defenders
articles.body:
L uka Doncic is making the extraordinary look almost routine. The Los Angeles Lakers superstar has opened the 2026-27 season with a scoring surge that briefly put him above 40 points per game, a threshold no player in NBA histor y has sustained over a full season except Wilt Chamberlain. The possibility alone puts the Slovenian superstar in rare company. But the more remarkable part is how effortlessly he appears to be getting his points. He can beat defenders off the dribble, create separation with a step-back, punish switches in the post, finish around the rim and find teammates when opposing defenses send extra help. There is no obvious answer to the question of how to guard him.

Through 16 games, Doncic is averaging 36.6 points, 6.6 rebounds and 7.7 assists. He has scored 586 points and is shooting 46 percent from the field, while making 4.8 three-pointers per game. Those numbers have already put him among the most prolific scorers in the league’s historical rankings, even though the season has barely begun.

His opening stretch was even more spectacular. After nine games, Luka was averaging 40.1 points, a pace that placed him alongside Chamberlain as the only players to reach that mark at that stage of a season. His 52-point performance against Utah in his third game helped establish the tone, and he followed it with a 53-point outing against Portland on November 6.

There is, of course, a considerable difference between producing those numbers in October and November and maintaining them through an 82-game schedule. Doncic knows that better than most. Last spring, he was on another remarkable scoring run before a hamstring injury forced him to miss the final two weeks of the regular season.

That is the biggest obstacle between the Slovenian star and a place in the record books: staying healthy long enough to make the numbers count.

Chamberlain remains the only member of the 40-point club

The history Luka is chasing is extraordinary. Chamberlain remains the only player to average at least 40 points per game over an entire NBA season. He accomplished the feat twice, averaging 50.4 points in 1961-62 and 44.8 in 1962-63.

No one has come close to those figures since. Michael Jordan’s 37.1 points per game in 1986-87 stands as the highest scoring average by a player other than Chamberlain. James Harden reached 36.1 in 2018-19, while Rick Barry averaged 35.6 in 1966-67 and Kobe Bryant finished with 35.4 in 2005-06.

Doncic's current 36.6-point average would already rank among the greatest scoring seasons ever if he could maintain it. He is also approaching a milestone that would be unprecedented for the Lakers franchise. No player in the team’s history has averaged 40 points per game over a full season.

The franchise has had some extraordinary offensive seasons. Elgin Baylor averaged 38.3 points in 1961-62, while Bryant’s 35.4 in 2005-06 remains one of the defining scoring campaigns of the modern Lakers era. Luka is threatening to take that legacy into uncharted territory.

The comparison with Harden’s 2018-19 season is particularly interesting. Both players combine heavy scoring responsibilities with elite playmaking, and both can dictate the rhythm of an offense for long stretches. Doncic is averaging nearly eight assists, meaning his production is not simply a matter of taking more shots. He is also responsible for creating opportunities for the players around him.

Why opposing defenses have no easy answer

At 6-foot-8, Doncic presents a difficult matchup for smaller guards. He can use his size to protect the ball, create space and shoot over defenders. Bigger players, meanwhile, often struggle to stay in front of him when he changes direction or attacks off the dribble.

His game is built around deception and control rather than explosive athleticism. Luka does not need to dominate above the rim or overwhelm defenders with speed. He uses hesitation moves, changes of pace and precise footwork to make opponents lose their balance. Once he creates even a small opening, he can turn it into a step-back three, a mid-range jumper or a drive to the basket.

The free-throw line is another important part of his scoring arsenal. Luka is attempting approximately 10 free throws per game, giving him another way to build his point total even when his outside shot is not falling. Defenses have increasingly abandoned the idea of assigning one player to guard him for an entire game. Instead, teams rotate defenders, send help and try to force the ball out of his hands.

But that approach carries its own risks. Doncic has the court vision to find the open man, and his passing can punish teams that commit too many players to stopping his scoring.

The Lakers’ offense belongs to Luka

One reason Doncic's production has reached another level is the amount of offensive responsibility he now carries. During his time in Dallas, he shared playmaking duties with Kyrie Irving . In Los Angeles, he spent much of his first two seasons alongside LeBron James, another player capable of initiating the offense and creating shots for teammates.

Under head coach JJ Redick, Doncic has become the central engine of the Lakers’ attack. His role, his conditioning and his competitive instincts have combined to produce a season that could become the best of his career. The supporting cast remains an important part of the equation. Reaves is averaging nearly 25 points per game and has emerged as a significant offensive partner.

There is also the question of what happens when the schedule becomes more demanding. The NBA season is a marathon, not a sprint. Travel, back-to-back games, physical defenses and the accumulated wear of an 82-game campaign can change a player’s trajectory quickly. Doncic’s hamstring injury last spring is a reminder that even the most unstoppable offensive player cannot control everything.

His MVP competition is another compelling storyline. Victor Wembanyama has emerged as a major challenger, and the two stars are expected to be central figures in the race as the season develops. Their November 27 meeting between the Lakers and San Antonio Spurs adds another chapter to that competition, with both teams pursuing a strong position in the West

articles.title: Bronny James receives a key announcement from JJ Redick ahead of the Lakers biggest game of the season
articles.standfirst: Bronny has appeared in seven of the Lakers' 18 games, playing a total of 18 minutes this season
articles.summary: Bronny has appeared in seven of the Lakers' 18 games, playing a total of 18 minutes this season
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers ( 15-3 ) enter Friday night’s NBA Cup clash against the San Antonio Spurs ( 15-4 ) at Frost Bank Center in what shapes up as their biggest test of the 2026-27 season so far.

Facing off between the two best records in basketball carries massive knockout-stage weight: a loss would knock the losing side almost immediately out of NBA Cup advancement contention, while the winner can lock in top positioning depending on how the Golden State Warriors and Portland Trail Blazers fare.

Los Angeles, led by early season MVP Luka Doncic, also gets a major health boost with zero players on the injury report , as Austin Reaves returns after missing the previous five games , whereas San Antonio has guards De’Aaron Fox and Dylan Harper listed as questionable.

Lakers Ship Bronny James to G League Ahead of Spurs Showdown

Before tipoff in San Antonio, the franchise announced another developmental move for Bronny James , assigning the 22-year-old guard to the Coachella Valley Lakers ahead of their upcoming slate on November 29 and December 3.

Through seven brief NBA appearances under head coach JJ Redick this season, averaging just 2.7 minutes per game, Bronny has put up 1.1 points per game with zero assists and zero rebounds , while posting a -34 plus-minus across roughly 18 total minutes on the floor, meaning Los Angeles has been outscored by 34 points during his short stretches.

With production and court time that scarce, cracking Redick’s nightly rotation has proven nearly impossible, even as Bronny averages 22.0 points , 4.0 rebounds , and 7.0 assists in the NBA G League .

That stark gap, looking too sharp for the minor-league level while still struggling to stick in the big league. keeps him firmly in the spotlight as the February NBA trade deadline draws closer.
